b: When the user wants to write or judge ad creative, or asks which ad, hook, or angle to run or kill: headlines, primary text, and variations for Google, Meta, LinkedIn, and TikTok, fresh angles when creative fatigues. Test hypotheses name the metric, comparison, and expected direction. No AI tells like 'it's not X, it's Y'. For campaign strategy, see ads. For landing pages, see copywriting.

When the user wants to get cited and recommended in AI answers (ChatGPT, Perplexity, AI Overviews), or asks why AI cites a competitor, which content gets cited, or whether llms.txt or a page format is worth it: AEO, GEO, AI visibility, agent-readable sites. For technical and on-page SEO, see seo-audit. For structured data, see schema.

When the user wants to reduce churn, or asks why customers cancel, whether to offer a discount or pause: cancellation flows, exit surveys, save offers, dunning and failed-payment recovery. For win-back emails, see emails. For in-app upgrade screens, see paywalls.

When the user wants to write or run B2B cold outbound, or asks whether an opener, reason to reach out, or email works or why nobody replies: cold emails, follow-ups, sending domains, deliverability, LinkedIn, cadences. Send from secondary domains, verify lists first, turn off open tracking, stop every channel when a prospect replies. No AI tells like 'it's not X, it's Y'. For the list, see prospecting. For lifecycle email, see emails. For call scripts, see sales-enablement.

When the user wants to plan content, or asks which topic or piece to prioritize, what to write about, or why posts bring no customers: topic clusters, editorial calendars, roadmaps tied to customers and search. For writing pieces, see copywriting. For SEO audits, see seo-audit. For social content, see social.

When the user wants to write or rewrite page copy (homepage, landing, pricing, feature), or asks which headline, promise, or message to lead with. Diagnoses the input first (blank brief, real voice, or point edit) and changes only what it calls for. Claims must be supportable; a declined claim names the evidence that would unlock it. No AI tells like 'it's not X, it's Y' or 'no X, no Y, no Z'. For editing, see copy-editing. For emails, see emails. For the offer, see offers.

When the user wants to plan or improve a lead magnet, or asks what to give away for emails or how much to ask in return (gating, form fields): checklists, templates, ebooks, gated guides, content upgrades. For interactive tools, see free-tools. For the follow-up sequence, see emails. For popups that capture emails, see popups.

When the user wants to apply psychology to marketing, or asks why buyers behave or value things as they do, or whether a persuasion tactic is honest: biases, mental models, anchoring, social proof, scarcity, loss aversion, framing. For a page, see cro. For pricing tactics, see pricing. For copy, see copywriting.

When the user wants SEO pages at scale from templates and data, or asks whether a page set will rank or look thin: location, integration, comparison, directory, and '[X] for [Y]' pages, each useful rather than thin. For SEO audits, see seo-audit. For content planning, see content-strategy.

Load this skill for any project with a user interface that must work across screen sizes and input methods, such as websites, web apps, dashboards, marketing pages, emails, or design systems. Use when building or reviewing layouts, choosing breakpoints, setting up fluid type, sizing touch targets, or making components adapt to their container. One design must serve phones, tablets, laptops, desktops, touch, mouse, and keyboard. Prefers content-first, mobile-first, framework-agnostic CSS and Baseline-stable features.

When the user wants to audit or diagnose SEO, or asks why traffic dropped, a page won't rank, or whether a setup like canonicals, hreflang, or redirects is right: technical SEO, indexing, Google updates, on-page and titles, Core Web Vitals, local SEO. Start here when someone just says their SEO is bad. For pages at scale, see programmatic-seo. For structured data, see schema. For AI search, see ai-seo.

Guided self-editing checklist for anyone writing an article, essay, story, email, or post. Turns a rough draft into clear, punchy, well-flowing prose by running it against the writer's intent, reader, and a set of concrete revision checks. Use when the user says "review my writing", "edit this draft", "make this clearer", "tighten this up", "writing checklist", "proofread", "polish this piece", or asks how to improve an article, story, essay, or copy.
